en: The CEO says, wow, that's a very interesting project.

en: They let them work on it for six months, 12 months, and it has an absolute interesting success, but not breakout and doesn't belong inside the first company.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: You can spin it out.

en: Second case.

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, we want to get hired, but maybe Washington DC doesn't exactly want us to sell a company and the shares in it.
zh: 嘿,我们想被雇用,但也许华盛顿特区不太希望我们直接卖掉一家公司以及其中的股份。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're gonna do an IP license and we're gonna spin it out that way.
zh: 所以我们要做一个 IP 许可,然后我们用那种方式把它分拆出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two different situations, very different.
zh: 两种不同的情况,非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's start with the first one.
zh: 让我们从第一种开始。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: The holding company took too much equity.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then every CEO is saying, why can't I leave and get 80% of this new company?
zh: 然后每个 CEO 都说,为什么他可以离开还拿到这家新公司 80% 的股权?

speaker: Unknown
en: This isn't fair.
zh: 这不公平。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should own 90% of the company and the co-founder leaving should get 10%.
zh: 我们应该拥有这家公司 90% 的股权,而离开的联合创始人应该拿 10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell us a little bit about spin-outs, why they happen, and then what's the best practice?
zh: 给我们讲讲分拆吧,为什么它们会发生,然后最佳实践是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you laid the groundwork perfectly.
zh: 我是说,你把背景铺垫得非常完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is what the situation where we see the spin-outs most often.
zh: 那确实是我们最常见到分拆的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: The why behind it might be, right, it's faster to start with that technology that has already been built and tested and validated and, like you said, may not just fit within that existing entity.
zh: 背后的原因可能是,对吧,从已经构建、测试并验证过的技术起步会更快,而且,就像你说的,它可能就是不适合留在那个现有实体内部。

speaker: Unknown
en: It may be distracting to what the goal is there.
zh: 它可能会分散那个实体对自身目标的注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: From an existing entity's perspective, if they're not going to use that technology or that asset going forward and they don't really want to put the funds to it or the resources toward it to scale and grow because it's maybe not in the direction of their strategic vision where they want that company to go, it may be more valuable to them to say, all right, well, you're interested in this.
zh: 从现有实体的角度来看,如果他们往后不打算使用那项技术或那个资产,而且他们真的不想投入资金或资源去把它规模化和发展,因为这也许不符合他们对那家公司战略方向的愿景,那么对他们来说,更划算的做法可能是说,好吧,你对这个感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I spin it out and I agree, I'll transfer X, Y, and Z over to you.
zh: 如果我把它分拆出去并且同意,我会把 X、Y、Z 转让给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: You go grow it, or maybe I'll get some benefit from that.
zh: 你去把它做大,或者也许我能从中获得一些好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's really the why behind it.
zh: 所以这就是它背后真正的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, these things take all kinds of shapes and sizes.
zh: 你知道,这些事情有各种各样的形态和规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, another example is that we see all the time is university, right?
zh: 哦,另一个我们随时都能见到的例子就是大学,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've got folks working at the university to do R&D, and they're like, whoa, we're on to something.
zh: 所以你有在大学里做研发的人，他们觉得，哇，我们有发现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is also a spin-out type situation where instead of negotiating with a company, you're negotiating with the university in terms of what are the terms going to look like, of how am I going to get that IP into a new co and be able to start a new venture.
zh: 那也是一种分拆出来的情形，只不过你不是和一家公司谈判，而是和大学谈判，就条款会是什么样子达成一致，即我如何把那个 IP 拿进一家新公司并能够开启一个新的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's a lot of considerations that go into how we would think about these and how we would structure them.
zh: 但有很多考量因素会影响我们如何看待这些事情以及如何构建它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are so fact-specific.
zh: 它们非常依赖具体事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first thing I'll say is like, this is going to be pretty high level and a lot more of, you should think about this and you should think about that.
zh: 所以我要说的第一件事是，这会相当高层，而且更多是「你应该考虑这个、你应该考虑那个」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's a few different ways to go about it rather than, oh, well, when you do this, you should do this and you should do that.
zh: 还有这里是几种不同的做法，而不是「哦，好，当你做这件事时，你就应该这样做、应该那样做」。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's, I don't know, I don't know what it should look like because there are just so many different sizes and how these things take form.
zh: 我不知道，我不知道它应该是什么样子，因为这些事情的规模和成形方式实在太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: When this happens, sometimes it's at a big company.
zh: 当这种情况发生时，有时是在一家大公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google has famously spun out Waymo, a very famous Microsoft back in the day, this little site Expedia that was internal.
zh: Google 有著名的 Waymo 分拆，很久以前 Microsoft 也有，那个内部的小网站 Expedia。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that can be for economic reasons or the things getting so big.
zh: 那可能是出于经济原因，或者是事情变得太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the existing management team is getting distracted by it.
zh: 而现有的管理团队正被它分散精力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Waymo needs to be out there on its own raising capital to validate its, from what I understand, the back channel I got was, hey, we need to validate this valuation.
zh: 而 Waymo 需要独立出去融资来验证它的，据我了解，我得到的背后消息是，嘿，我们需要验证这个估值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in order to get AI talent to work on a self-driving company, they, you know, were up against Anthropic or X, SpaceX, XI, or
zh: 而且为了让 AI 人才来一家自动驾驶公司工作，他们，你知道的，面对的是 Anthropic 或 X、SpaceX、XI，或者

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenAI, we need a currency where people can say, oh, this is going to be a trillion-dollar company.
zh: OpenAI，我们需要一种货币，让人们可以说，哦，这将会是一家万亿美元的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there is a real reason to spin it out.
zh: 所以分拆出来是有实际理由的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like to run a little test when I talk to the two founders.
zh: 我和两位创始人交谈时喜欢做一个小测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I say to them, what's an amount where if this thing spun out and it became a unicorn?
zh: 我对他们说，如果这个东西分拆出来变成了一家独角兽，什么样的金额——

speaker: Unknown
en: You would feel great about the terms that we got to.
zh: 会让我们最终谈成的条款让你感觉很好？

speaker: Unknown
en: And typically, I tell people, have the existing company keep 20%.
zh: 通常，我会告诉人们，让原公司保留 20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let the new team keep 80%.
zh: 让新团队保留 80%。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to go 51, 40, whatever.
zh: 他们想 51、40，随便什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes it's 25, 75, 30, 70.

speaker: Unknown
en: It is specific because maybe the thing's making $0 and losing money.
zh: 这是具体情况具体分析，因为也许这个东西收入为零还在亏钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes it's making some money.
zh: 有时它在赚一些钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's all kinds of provisions you can do.
zh: 所以有各种各样的条款安排可以做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you look at that,
zh: 但当你看那个结果时，

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost universally, if it becomes a billion-dollar outcome, the company that spun it out, getting 20% of a billion-dollar company, you feel pretty smart, pretty savvy for having done that.

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you take 50%, 60%, and it goes to zero, well, you're like, well, that was dumb.
zh: 但如果你拿 50%、60%，而它归零了，那么，你会觉得，那可真蠢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for the co-founder, if he were to spin it out, they got 60%, 70%, 80% of the company, were able to build a team, raise more funding.
zh: 而对于联合创始人来说，如果他把它分拆出来，他们拿到了公司的 60%、70%、80%，能够组建团队、融更多资。

speaker: Unknown
en: That wouldn't feel so bad paying that 20%.
zh: 那么付出那 20% 也不会感觉太糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey.
zh: 嘿。

speaker: Unknown
en: We chose to do that.
zh: 是我们选择这么做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could have left and just built it ourselves, yeah?
zh: 我们本可以离开然后自己把它做出来，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's sometimes you have to take people through, well, here's the possible outcomes.
zh: 所以有时你必须带人们过一遍，好，这里是可能的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you do that where you say, here are scenarios?
zh: 你会那样做吗，你说，这里是几种情景？

speaker: Unknown
en: And people ask their attorneys, like, can you play out some scenarios for me so I understand, like?
zh: 而人们会问他们的律师，比如，你能帮我推演一些情景吗，好让我理解，像是——

speaker: Unknown
en: What's at the other side of the rainbow, practically speaking?
zh: 从实际角度来说，彩虹的另一端是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The consideration often takes the form of equity.
zh: 对价通常采取股权的形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can also be cash.
zh: 它也可以是现金。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes it's a combination of cash and equity.
zh: 有时是现金和股权的组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you start getting into more complex structures, you might see earnouts based on milestones or royalties.
zh: 如果你开始进入更复杂的结构，你可能会看到基于里程碑的盈利支付或特许权使用费。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll often see those in connection with IP being spun out of universities.
zh: 我们经常在与大学分拆出来的 IP 相关的交易中看到这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when it is equity, because that is where oftentimes where the
zh: 但当它是股权时，因为那往往是——

speaker: Unknown
en: Either all or a big chunk of the consideration is going to be.
zh: 要么全部、要么很大一部分对价所在的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's negotiations definitely around the percentage, but also around what class of stock are you going to get?
zh: 围绕比例肯定有谈判，但也会围绕你将拿到哪一类股票？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you getting common?
zh: 你拿到的是普通股吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you getting preferred?
zh: 你拿到的是优先股吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What rights go with that stock?
zh: 那只股票附带哪些权利？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you getting information rights?
zh: 你会拿到信息知情权吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you getting pro rata rights?
zh: 你会拿到按比例跟投权吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether you want a board seat or a board observer.
zh: 无论你是想要一个董事会席位还是董事会观察员席位。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about that on another one of these.
zh: 我们在其中另一期里聊过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of those things, kind of that as the package of things,
zh: 所有这些事情，差不多作为一个整体的打包，

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody does focus in on that percentage.
zh: 每个人都会把焦点集中在那个百分比上。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other stuff is like, kind of like, okay, well, we'll deal with that.
zh: 其他 stuff 就像是，好吧，那个我们到时候再处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the percentage really matters.
zh: 但那个百分比真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I will say there's not a market range.
zh: 而我要说的是，这没有一个市场区间。

speaker: Unknown
en: It varies, varies a ton, but I will say
zh: 它变化非常大，但我要说，

speaker: Unknown
en: If it gets to be too large, that's where you are going to have potential problems going forward in new code.
zh: 如果它变得太大，那才是你在往后新的 code 中会遇到潜在问题的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Investors, I imagine the reason you're spinning this out is it's going to get spun out.
zh: 投资人，我猜你们要把这个 spin 出来的原因是，它反正要被 spin 出去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever group of employees are going over there, they're going to grow it.
zh: 无论哪一群员工过去那边，他们都会把它做大。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to go ask investors to make an investment over there and hopefully it becomes that unicorn.
zh: 他们会去请投资人到那边做投资，希望它能变成那只独角兽。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order for investors to get excited about NuCo and making an investment in NuCo, they want to know the founders are motivated.
zh: 为了让投资人对 NuCo 兴奋、愿意投资 NuCo，他们想知道创始人们是有动力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The founders...
zh: 创始人们……

speaker: Unknown
en: Are invested here.
zh: 在这里有投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the old company, I'll call it parent or existing company, has an 80% stake or a 50% stake in the company and the founders have smaller stakes, they're probably less motivated.
zh: 如果老公司，我姑且叫它母公司或现有公司，在这家公司持有 80% 或 50% 的股份，而创始人们的股份较小，那他们的动力可能就没那么足。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the same in any.
zh: 在任何情况下都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if you're not doing a spin now, that's the same of any investment analysis at the early days is by an investor.
zh: 即使你现在不做 spin，这在早期对投资人来说也是任何投资分析的共同点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's like, I want you to grow this company.
zh: 就是说，我要你把这家公司做大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want you to drive long-term growth.

speaker: Unknown
en: I want you to be excited about that.
zh: 我要你为此感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have a small stake, you may not be.
zh: 如果你只有很小的股份，你可能不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't break the cap table is, I think, we see it coming into, we will have sometimes somebody comes into the accelerator and they gave 25% of the company to the people who built the app, the first version, fully vested.
zh: 「别搞坏 cap table」，我认为，我们见过它走进来，有时候有人进入加速器，他们把公司 25% 的股份给了那些做出 app 第一个版本的人，而且已完全 vest。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have to tell them, you're never going to clear market with investors.
zh: 我们不得不告诉他们，你永远过不了投资人的市场关。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't have you in the accelerator if you don't have a chance of pulling through.
zh: 如果你没有通关的机会，我们不能让你进加速器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why don't you go to them, say you'll give them $50,000 and two points in common shares.
zh: 你为什么不去找他们，说你会给他们 5 万美元和两个点的普通股。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if it was going to cost them $100,000 to build the app, you're giving them $50,000 in cash and two points in common, and you have the right to buy those back at a $10 million valuation so they can make $250,000 and they, wow, you guys are suckers for spending $250,000 building the first version of the app.
zh: 所以如果建这个 app 要花他们 10 万美元，你就给他们 5 万美元现金加两个点的普通股，并且你有权以 1000 万美元估值买回那些股份，这样他们能赚到 25 万美元，然后他们，哇，你们这帮人花 25 万美元建 app 第一个版本真是冤大头。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd say when we give them the right
zh: 我要说，当我们给他们那个权利的

speaker: Unknown
en: Language, it works more than half the time, maybe 60% of the time, but it doesn't work 100% of the time.
zh: 条款时，它一半以上的情况都管用，也许 60% 的情况，但它不是 100% 管用。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why it's important to have a great attorney and think these things through before and understand the basics.
zh: 这就是为什么有一位出色的律师很重要，并且要提前把这些事情想清楚、理解基本原理。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's happening with all these licensing deals?
zh: 这些 licensing 交易到底是怎么回事？

speaker: Unknown
en: That seemed to me to be something that under a previous administration where M&A was being stifled.
zh: 在我看来，那似乎是上一届政府时期的东西，当时 M&A 被压制了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they weren't as in favor of it as opposed to maybe the world we're living in today.
zh: 他们不像也许我们今天所处的世界那样支持它。

speaker: Unknown
en: No politics here, but just the game on the field.
zh: 这里不谈政治，只谈场上的比赛。

speaker: Unknown
en: People got creative.
zh: 人们变得有创意了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They said, hey, you want this team on your team?
zh: 他们说，嘿，你想要这个团队加入你的团队？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you want them there tomorrow?
zh: 而且你想让他们明天就在那儿？

speaker: Unknown
en: You want them working there Monday?
zh: 你想让他们周一就在那儿工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's Thursday.
zh: 现在是周四。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll be on site Monday?
zh: 他们周一就能到位？

speaker: Unknown
